title: Choosing the 'only when' condition
idea: Pick the condition that selects exactly the passes a problem wants to act on.

exercises.prompt: 'For each number 1 to 20, print it only when it is a multiple of 10.' Which condition?
exercises.explanation: A multiple of 10 has remainder 0: i % 10 == 0. That matches 10 and 20.

exercises.prompt: Which numbers print for that multiple-of-10 loop over 1..20?
exercises.explanation: 10 and 20 are the multiples of 10 up to 20.

exercises.prompt: 'Add up only the numbers from 1 to 10 that are 5 or more.' Which condition?
What is that total (numbers 5..10 from the 1..10 loop)?
Match each 'only when' phrase to its condition.
exercises.explanation: Translate the plain-English rule into the comparison that selects exactly those passes.

exercises.prompt: Which numbers print for that 'below 4' loop over 1..10?
Arrange a loop that prints only numbers 1..10 that are NOT equal to 5.
exercises.explanation: for header, the if with !=, then the indented print.

exercises.prompt: How many numbers print for that 'not equal to 5' loop over 1..10?
exercises.explanation: All ten except 5 — that is nine numbers.

exercises.prompt: Why is choosing the RIGHT condition the heart of an 'only when' problem?
options: It selects exactly which passes act
exercises.explanation: The condition decides exactly which passes act; a wrong one acts on the wrong passes and gives a wrong result.
